extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and practitioners handling ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements for proposing, presenting, and processing amendments (specification, claims, drawings), fee obligations for added claims, and related procedural requirements in USPTO reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and effectiveness of proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments proposed in a reexamination will normally be entered and be considered to be entered for purposes of prosecution before the Office (if they are timely and comply with the rules); however, the amendments do not become effective in the patent until the reexamination certificate under 35 U.S.C. 307 is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment will be permitted where the certificate issues after expiration of the patent (see 37 CFR 1.530(d)(3)). Patent expiration date must account for patent term, maintenance fees, disclaimers, term extensions/adjustments under 35 U.S.C. 154 and 156, and any other relevant information. Amendments that comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and are formally presented under 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b) and accompanied by required fees (37 CFR 1.20(c)) will be entered pursuant to MPEP § 2234. Examiner’s amendments are treated specially (the 1.121(g) exception does not apply in reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal presentation requirements for amendment papers
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendment papers to be part of the permanent USPTO file must comply with the formal requirements of 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b); 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(k) uniquely apply to amendments in reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adding claims, excess claim fees per 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (4) may apply. Submissions must comply regardless of medium (paper or compact disc under 1.96 or 1.825). Failure to comply may lead to informal response, non-entry of the amendment, or termination of prosecution (see PTOL forms guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment format (37 CFR 1.530(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the reexamination specification (other than claims/drawings) must be made by submission of the full text of any paragraph to be changed, with markings (brackets for deletions and underlining for additions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presenting its text. All paragraphs added must be submitted as completely underlined. The precise point where each amendment is to be made must be indicated. Markings are always made vis-à-vis the original patent (not relative to prior amendments). Requirement applies irrespective of filing medium. Examiner’s amendments at NIRC preparation also require full text with markings (1.121(g) exception does not apply). Blocked paragraph insertion (letter/number and caret) is used so page formatting need not be a concern. Examples are provided in the MPEP to illustrate proper paragraph replacement formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment and presentation rules (37 CFR 1.530(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim proposed to be amended, the entire text of the claim must be presented with appropriate markings; for each proposed new claim, the entire text must be presented and underlined throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent claim canceled is canceled by direction (no need to present the text in brackets). A previously added new claim canceled is canceled by direction. Examiner’s amendments at NIRC time also require full claim text with markings; 1.121(g) exception does not apply. Markings: underlining for added material and single brackets for deleted material (1.530(f)). Original patent claims may not be renumbered; added claims must be numbered beginning after the last original patent claim. Presentation rules apply regardless of paper or electronic medium. Examples in MPEP show amended claim formatting. If dependency of an original claim is changed, it’s proper to make that original claim dependent on a later-filed higher-numbered claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status and explanation requirement (37 CFR 1.530(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendment submitted must set forth the status of all patent claims and all added claims as of the date of submission (whether pending or canceled) and must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claim status will generally result in a notification to patent owner of an informal response (see MPEP § 2266.02) prior to final rejection. Failure to submit the explanation of support will generally result in a notification that the amendment prior to final rejection is not completely responsive because omission goes to the merits (see MPEP § 2266.01). Amendments submitted after final rejection will not be entered. Patent owners must point out what is changed in the “Remarks” portion of the amendment when amending previously added claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings are relative to the original patent, not prior amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All bracketing and underlining is made in comparison to the original patent; not in comparison with the prior amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing second or subsequent amendments, include prior changes previously presented in earlier amendments (as part of the full claim/paragraph text) and indicate only changes vis-à-vis the original. Words added in earlier amendments that are later deleted are not shown in brackets in subsequent amendments (they are simply omitted). Examples (knife/cutting means) in MPEP illustrate formatting across multiple amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering rules for original and added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims may not be renumbered; a patent claim retains its number even if canceled in reexamination, and numbering of any added claims must begin after the last original patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new claim number assigned to a new claim is later canceled, that previously assigned number should not be reused for a different new claim during the reexamination proceeding. At time of preparing the NIRC, remaining new claims will be renumbered in numerical order to follow highest original claim number for issuance on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and amendment of new claims (claims not in patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed new claim must be presented with underlining throughout; an amendment of a new claim must present the entire text of the new claim containing the amendatory material, underlined throughout, and cannot contain any bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because changes are made vis-à-vis the original patent, the presentation of an amended new claim does not indicate what changed from a previous version; patent owner must point out what is changed in the “Remarks” portion. Each change must be accompanied by explanation of support in the disclosure (37 CFR 1.530(e)). Examples are given of proper presentation. The presentation cannot show prior-version bracketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment procedure (37 CFR 1.530(d)(3) and §1.84 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner; upon approval, new sheets of drawings including the changes and complying with §1.84 must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended figures must be identified as “Amended,” added figures as “New,” and canceled figures must be surrounded by brackets and identified as “Canceled.” Changes may NOT be made on the original patent drawings. The sketch is made part of the record. Examiner may have draftsperson review new sheets; draftsperson’s stamp is no longer required. New sheets must be entered into the record prior to NIRC preparation. If sketch approved but new sheets not filed and proceeding is otherwise in condition for NIRC, prepare Quayle action setting one month SSP for filing new sheets; failure to timely file will result in reexamination certificate issued with drawings that do not reflect the proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on proposing amendments to expired patents (37 CFR 1.530(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent; if a patent expires during the pendency of a reexamination, all amendments to the patent claims and all claims added during the proceeding are withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawn amendments are carried out by placing a diagonal line across all amended and new claims (and added specification text) residing in amendment papers. Patent owner should be notified in next Office action. Office action will hold amendments to be improper and state subsequent reexamination will be on basis of unamended patent claims. Only cancellation of original patent claims is permitted after expiration. Examiner should ensure all rejected and objected-to claims are canceled at time NIRC is to be issued; examiner may issue examiner’s amendment canceling such claims not already canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of changes vis-à-vis prior proceedings/certificates (making all changes vis-à-vis the patent being reexamined)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the patent being reexamined must be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination; reexamination certificate print shows underlined matter in italics and brackets as inserted during the proceeding (37 CFR 1.530(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent was previously changed via a prior reexamination certificate, reissue, certificate of correction, etc., the first amendment must be made relative to the patent specification as changed by that prior proceeding; all subsequent amendments are also made relative to the specification as of the request filing date (not relative to prior amendments). For making amendments in a pending reexamination where a prior certificate or reissue exists, italicized text of certificate/reissue is treated as present without italics in the original patent and bracketed text is considered omitted. See MPEP §§ 2295, 2285, etc. for merged proceedings handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and examples for common amendment actions (presentation, cancellation, multiple amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP provides detailed examples showing proper formats: replacing a specification paragraph with underlining/bracketing; amending claims (showing bracketed deletions and underlined additions); canceling original patent claims by written direction; presenting new claims underlined; amending original patent claims more than once must include previous changes and new changes in the full-text presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: how to present a replaced paragraph; how to amend claim 6 with bracketed deletions and underlined additions; canceling claim(s) by 'Cancel claim X.'; adding claim 7 underlined; handling sequential amendments where earlier-added word (e.g., 'bone') is later deleted and thus not bracketed in second amendment; show that all amendments are compared to original patent text only. These examples illustrate anti-patterns (e.g., showing changes relative to prior amendment rather than original) and proper formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical handling and cross-references for merged and special proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references to other MPEP sections govern clerical handling and special situations: MPEP §2270 for clerical handling (ex parte reexamination), §2670 for inter partes, §2283 for merged ex parte proceedings, §2285 for ex parte merged with reissue, and §§2686.01/.03 for inter partes involvement in mergers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reexamination is merged with other proceedings (reissue, another reexam), amendments must be presented as if the prior changes (e.g., certificate italics) are part of the original patent per the cited MPEP sections. These cross-references guide examiners and practitioners on correct clerical and procedural handling in complicated procedural contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination (37 CFR 1.530(l) and §1.324)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the correct inventor(s) were not named through error without deceptive intent, the Director may, on petition of all required parties and satisfactory proof and payment of fee per §1.324 and §1.20(b), include an amendment naming only the actual inventor(s) in the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be submitted as part of the reexamination proceeding and satisfy §1.324. If petition is granted, the inventorship change is merged into the reexamination certificate. If the reexamination concludes without issuance of a reexamination certificate (e.g., vacated or denied), the patent owner may request a certificate of correction indicating change of inventorship. Alternatively, correction by reissue under 35 U.S.C. 251 may be appropriate (see MPEP §1412.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for filing reexamination requests and excess-claims fees (37 CFR 1.20(c) and 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees: filing a request for ex parte reexamination (§1.510(a)) — $2,520.00; filing a request for inter partes reexamination (§1.915(a)) — $8,800.00. Excess claims fees apply for claims added in reexamination per 37 CFR 1.20(c): independent-claims fee for each independent claim in excess of three and in excess of number of independents in patent (small entity $100; other than small $200); total-claims fee for each claim in excess of twenty and of the number in patent (small entity $25; other than small $50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess claims fees became applicable to reexamination amendments filed on or after December 8, 2004 (per amendment implementing 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2)). Excess claims fees apply only to new (excess) claims. A claim disclaimed under 35 U.S.C. 253 or canceled via prior reexamination certificate, reissue, or certificate of correction as of the request filing date is not considered part of the patent for fee calculations. Examples illustrate various cancellation/addition scenarios to determine fees due. If excess claims fees are not paid when due, a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-475) will issue with a one-month time period (extensions per 37 CFR 1.550(c) may be requested); failure to pay results in termination/abandonment of prosecution under 37 CFR 1.550(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-deficiency and procedural consequences (PTOL-475, PTOL-473, PTOL-467)
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess-claims fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c) are not paid with presentation of excess claims, the Office issues a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-475) with a one-month time period to correct; failure to timely correct will lead to termination of the reexamination proceeding under 37 CFR 1.550(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-475 is a Notice of Defective Paper in Ex Parte Reexamination used for fee deficiencies; a cover sheet PTOL-473 is used for mailing notification to patent owner. If an informal amendment is submitted after final rejection, PTOL-475 and form paragraph 22.13 should not be used; instead issue advisory Office action using PTOL-467 indicating the amendment was not entered. Extensions of time to correct fee deficiencies may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). Termination results in issuance of a reexamination certificate or abandonment as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply rights of third-party requester (37 CFR 1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to the patent owner’s statement under §1.530 may be filed by the ex parte reexamination requester within two months from the date of service of the patent owner’s statement; any reply must be served on the patent owner in accordance with §1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 304 allows no extensions of time. If the patent owner does not file a statement under §1.530, no reply or other submission from the ex parte requester will be considered. The reply need not be limited to issues raised in the statement and may include additional prior art patents/printed publications and may raise any issue appropriate for reexamination.
